newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis wound seven Palestinians in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israelis wound seven Palestinians in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli soldiers shot and wounded at least seven Palestinians on Friday during clashes with Arab demonstrators as fresh violence erupted in the divided West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said.

They said about 50 Palestinian youths took part in the clashes, hurling dozens of fire bombs and home-made stun bombs of baking soda and water at soldiers across the invisible line that divides Hebron into Israeli- and PLO-controlled zones.
Soldiers fought back with rubber bullets, wounding at least seven, witnesses said. The clashes tapered off by early afternoon.
An Israeli army spokeswoman said Palestinian demonstrators threw firebombs and stones in the Hebron casbah and that security forces dispersed them with no casualties to Israeli troops.

Israel handed over most of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule in January but kept troops in about 20 percent of the city to guard some 400 Jewish settlers who live and study in fortified enclaves in the heart of the city of 100,000 Palestinians.
The dividing line has become a scene of regular confrontations since the handover.

More than 150 Palestinians and a number of Israeli soldiers were wounded during clashes in June after a U.S. congressional decision which demanded President Bill Clinton recognise Arab East Jerusalem as part of Israel's capital.
The violence came against the backdrop of a freeze in Israeli-PLO peacemaking following Israel's groundbreaking in March on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Israel captured East Jerusalem along with the rest of the West Bank in 1967 and later annexed it over international objections. Palestinians want East Jerusalem as capital of a future state.
